The Firm describes the two exposures as mirror images. In resale and securities borrowed agreements, it is exposed to credit risk to the extent that the value of the securities received is less than the initial cash principal advanced and any collateral amounts exchanged [1]. In repurchase and securities loaned agreements, credit risk exposure arises to the extent that the value of the underlying securities advanced exceeds the value of the initial cash principal received, and any collateral amounts exchanged [1]. Both are mitigated by monitoring the value of the underlying securities against cash proceeds and exchanged collateral, and requesting additional collateral or returning securities or collateral when appropriate [1]. The Firm also typically uses master netting agreements, which allow liquidation of the securities and collateral if a counterparty defaults [1]. For resale and securities borrowed agreements, it is Firm policy to take possession of the underlying securities where possible [1]. Because of these practices, the Firm held no allowance for credit losses on resale and securities borrowed arrangements as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 [2].

Alphabet uses a value-at-risk (VaR) analysis to determine the potential effect of interest rate fluctuations on its investment portfolio. Specifically, it uses a variance/covariance VaR model with a 95% confidence interval [2]. VaR is defined as the expected loss in fair value, for a given confidence interval, for the investment portfolio due to adverse movements in interest rates [2]. The resulting estimated one-day loss in fair value (interest rate risk category) was $208 million as of December 31, 2024 and $162 million as of December 31, 2025 [1].

Amazon's fiscal 2023 MD&A defines both measures in the footnotes to its foreign exchange table. The 'Exchange Rate Effect' is the change in reported amounts resulting from changes in foreign exchange rates from those in effect in the comparable prior year period for operating results [4]. The figures 'At Prior Year Rates' (the constant-rate figures) represent the outcome that would have resulted had foreign exchange rates in the reported period been the same as those in effect in the comparable prior year period for operating results [4]. The filing does not use the exact phrase 'at constant foreign exchange rates'; it uses 'At Prior Year Rates' and 'excluding the effect of foreign exchange rates' [1][5]. In its fiscal year 2024 10-K risk factors, Microsoft says that protecting its intellectual property rights and combating unlicensed copying and use of its software, source code, and other intellectual property on a global basis is difficult [2]. In its fiscal 2023 10-K, Amazon says it has agreements with vendors to receive consideration primarily for cooperative marketing efforts, promotions, incentives, and volume rebates [2]. It generally treats these amounts as a reduction of the prices it pays for goods (including property and equipment) or services, and records them as a reduction of the cost of inventory, cost of services, or cost of property and equipment [2]. Volume rebates typically depend on reaching minimum purchase thresholds, and Amazon evaluates the likelihood of reaching those thresholds using past experience and current year forecasts [2]. When volume rebates can be reasonably estimated, Amazon records a portion of the rebate as it makes progress towards the purchase threshold, which means it recognizes part of the rebate before the threshold is fully reached [2].
